baseline-one-player.qualification: Actual campaign geometry on one Windows machine. A one-player control is not network evidence. Observed callback/tic gaps include lockstep waiting and shared hardware contention where applicable. They are not displayed-frame or separate-machine performance.

qualification: Every recorded process uses the same Windows machine. Native state agreement is limited to the recorded observations. RenderOverlay gaps are not presented frames. Instrumented timings are sampled diagnostics, not release rendering acceptance.
findings: The pre-V5.12 two-peer clock returns before advancing the world. Its direct-deployment baseline has matching combatant counts but no sampled thermal or contamination advances; it is not behavior-equivalent to current multiplayer.
Current sampled clock cost is 1.3222/1.4357 ms over 41 samples per peer; NPC tick inclusive cost is 1088.4544/1104.848 ms. The scopes overlap and must not be summed.
Current two-peer siege callback tails remain severe. No production feature was disabled or new optimization claimed.

One-player controls have identical recorded census, aggregate NPC health and player positions; both retain severe siege callback stalls. These controls are not network tests or a measured regression clearance.

single_player_control.qualification: One observation per version; matching recorded census/health/positions is not whole-state equivalence. Neither proves rendering acceptance.
